lead_headline: Taco John's closure confirmed after 20+ years in Globeville — final lead in weekend's 11-lead sweep

restaurant.blurb: 11 new leads since Friday: Lost Coffee (Arvada), Moore. Cafe (Lakewood), Taco John's (Globeville closure confirmed), Denver Café & Kava (Park Hill kava bar), Tacos el Comando (Aurora shuttered), Petunia Bakeshop (Sunnyside relocation).

liquor.blurb: The blackout completes its eleventh day with zero new applications since the April 29-30 flood dumped 2,144 renewals into the system. The 7-day window remains flatlined at 0 versus last week's 2,386-application deluge — a complete collapse from the typical 20-30 weekly baseline. No official communication from state licensing on queue restoration or whether backend reconciliation continues. The freeze now stretches across two full weeks with no pipeline visibility, suggesting applications remain held offline awaiting batch release or caught in post-flood cleanup. May's licensing calendar stays completely dark as the Monday workweek opens with no sign of system recovery.

reputation.blurb: 1 mention yesterday (Jay's Garage classic car feature in Denver Post) keeps the weekend quiet, but the 7-day total climbs to 51 across 7 sources — up 19% from last week's 43. Denver Post commands 35% share with 18 mentions, followed by Instagram (13) and Facebook (6), with real estate and social coverage anchoring the week. The 51-mention tally runs 19% above last week and 8% ahead of the 30-day rolling average — outlets sustain elevated engagement heading into the Monday news cycle. Google News RSS drives 50 of 51 discoveries, maintaining baseline pickup consistency despite weekend lull. Week-over-week growth accelerates as editorial momentum builds from last week's 43-mention floor.

subscriptions.blurb: Net −2 since Friday (0 new, 2 canceled) pulls MTD to +15 (+1.5/day) while 90-day net holds at +134. The weekend flatlined on acquisition with zero new subscribers across Saturday and Sunday, while two Friday cancellations marked the only churn. This week's +10 net (15 new, 5 canceled) still reverses last week's +3 (25 new, 22 canceled), but the pattern shifts — acquisition volumes compress 40% week-over-week (15 vs 25) even as churn improves 77% (5 vs 22). MTD's +1.5/day rate runs 15% ahead of YTD's +1.3/day baseline, absorbing the weekend's zero-growth stall without structural damage. The trend suggests tighter inbound flow replacing last week's high-churn volume model, with retention stabilizing at lower absolute subscriber counts.
